First, we rewrite the polynomial, interpreting any constants as multiples of the identity matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(X) & ={X}^{2}+3X+2 \\  & ={X}^{2}+3X+2I\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find $f(H)={H}^{2}+3H+2I.$

Let's calculate ${H}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}^{2} & =H\cdot H \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 \\ 6 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can evaluate $f(H):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(H) & ={H}^{2}+3H+2I \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 \\ 6 & -2\end{aligned}]+3[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}]+2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 \\ 6 & -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}9 & -3 \\ 6 & 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7+9+2 & -3+(-3)+0 \\ 6+6+0 & -2+0+2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}18 & -6 \\ 12 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
